title: Hines's trumpet-style piano and Louis Armstrong
summary: Hines said he adapted trumpet ideas to piano.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Earl's very sensitive about, you know, through the years writers have said, you know, he played that trumpet style, and it's like what Louie Armstrong played, and that he really got that from Louie Armstrong. And Earl was very quick to deny this. And said that Louie got a lot of ideas from him. God only knows what the truth is, doesn't make too much difference, anyway.

Well, I've heard Earl say on an interview one time that he got his style from different trumpet players. He always wanted to play trumpet, and he couldn't play trumpet, so he just adapted it to the piano. And that's what he told us. And that's the only thing I can see -- I can see the similarity, with his right hand, you know.
The ideas are sometimes very much like Louie's ideas.
Well, thank God we had both of them. Those records they made together --
Those records they made together was beautiful.
Just like so far ahead of its time, you know, compared to what else was going on at that time, the recordings.
